Use its readable typography hierarchy and plant/copy relationship as supporting guidance. Its gray ovals and neutral colors are placeholders, not artwork to reproduce. No exact coordinate or pixel-size preservation is required. Produce the complete new colored graphic poster and all final typography natively.

Whole design: a mature, exuberant botanical paper-cut composition. Large real growing plant silhouettes open a ragged passage through the page: a broad-leaved potted tree enters heavily from the left crop, tall narrow attached sword leaves rise from a substantial pot at the far right, and a shorter leafy potted plant projects into the unused ragged right edge of the five-line prose. Show distinct connected stems, leaf growth, visible pot rims and soil surfaces, credible attachment and support. These are large angular cut-paper botanical forms, with incisive leaf lobes, cut negative spaces and controlled flat color layering. Their varied growth silhouettes embody the pleasure of choosing living plants of different sizes and tending them at home. They actively interlock the varying copy footprints from top to bottom; do not reduce them to a decorative outer border around a rectangular text panel. The short plant must be substantial alongside the body, while leaving every character clear. The page opening widens around the title and paired visit rows and tightens naturally at the short ends of the prose. Large leaf/pot masses are cropped at the page edges with deliberate abrupt boundaries; stems terminate visibly in their own pots.

Color/finish: deep blue-green and lighter blue-green foliage, citron leaf planes, mineral coral pottery, warm ivory negative space, dark pine-black copy. Color is carried by the active botanical cut shapes. Clean sharp flat paper-cut edges and sparse consistent paper fiber inside the larger colored shapes; precise flat ink typography. No soft blobs, rounded toy/clay plants, cute character clipart, pseudo handwriting, 3D room, framed artwork, gradients or arbitrary tape fragments. No extra decorative mark beside letters. No glyphs on pots or labels.

Typography and reading: the actual Korean Title is the immediate primary typographic anchor at the top entrance of the central passage, substantially larger and more prominent than ALL supporting text. Use generous mature Korean Myungjo/serif anatomy with sturdy thin strokes, open counters, stable syllable proportions and coherent serif stroke contrast. Keep the Title on one clear line. Small compatible semibold sans market eyebrow sits immediately above it; a restrained uppercase serif English companion immediately below. Subtitle uses a clear compatible semibold Korean sans. Title, subtitle and five-line body share one central left start (roughly 27% from the left). Set the body in the same mature serif anatomy, comfortably large and clean: roughly a readable 17–18px apparent body at a 720px-wide usage view, normal word spaces, moderate tracking, consecutive meaning-preserving lines and about 1.25 line spacing. Do not inflate word spacing to justify lines. The ending of the body leads directly downward to practical information at the same start, with short local gaps for functional turns. First pair date with hours on one baseline; next pair venue with free entry/repotting demonstration on one baseline; then care line, invitation line and URL directly below. Practical lines use one consistent compatible medium sans, around 15–16px apparent at 720px width, strong contrast, consistent numeral/Latin widths and baselines. Keep the paragraph and the useful visit/participation information visually adjacent and comfortably readable. No separate tiny footer or distant text islands.

Print ONLY the following supplied copy, each entry exactly ONCE. Preserve all Korean, Latin capitals, digits, word spaces, punctuation, ampersand, middle dots and the original en dashes. The following five consecutive prose lines are one paragraph with soft wraps at word boundaries; all other listed lines are separate entries. Do not print role names or add any new heading, bullet, pipe, arrow, plant tag, logo, watermark, QR or microtext.
